sources.citation: Henson, Bonnie Jean. 2007. The Phonology and Morphosyntax of Kol. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley (chair Larry M. Hyman). xx+592 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing: the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the 617-page text layer (0 hits). Ch. 2 Phonology (pp. 19-59) describes 32 consonants, 8 vowels with phonemic length, and two underlying tones H and L with HL/LH contours (pp. 19, 21), plus grammatical tones, tone rules (spreading, downstep, optional H absorption, polar tone, pp. 51-59) and an intonational phrase-final pitch lowering (p. 50). No statement on word prominence, metrical structure, or stress.

sources.citation: Henson, Bonnie Jean (2009). The phonology and morphosyntax of Kol. UMI.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No catalog record exists for Kol. The dissertation contributes a tonal description only (two underlying tones, contour tones, downstep, phrase-final intonational lowering) and says nothing about word stress, so it neither agrees with nor contradicts anything; it supports classing Kol as a tone language with no stress statement.
